text: Planning API backend unavailable :: The planning API crashed, was OOM-killed, or became unresponsive, so it could not accept connections from service:gridcast:grid-operator. :: Most likely, because a single consumer reporting PlanningApiUnreachable often points to the dependency itself being down or restarting.

Network path or firewall change :: A routing, firewall, or security-group change dropped or blocked traffic between service:gridcast:grid-operator and the planning API. :: Common cause of one-way unreachability where the API remains healthy but the network path fails.

DNS or service discovery failure :: Name resolution for the planning API returned no record, a stale IP, or SERVFAIL, so grid-operator could not obtain a valid endpoint. :: Fits a short transient outage and can affect only some clients depending on cached DNS.

Load balancer or ingress failure :: The load balancer or ingress in front of the planning API lost healthy backend targets or misrouted traffic, causing refused/reset connections. :: Plausible if planning API instances were healthy but the front door became unavailable.

Grid-operator client-side issue :: service:gridcast:grid-operator had a stale endpoint configuration, expired TLS client certificate, or exhausted connection pool, making the planning API appear unreachable. :: Less likely, but possible if the fault was isolated to the grid operator rather than the API or network.
